findings.title: Password check can be skipped with backup code + dummy totpCode
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts authorize() verifies the password only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121), but verifies a backup code whenever `credentials.backupCode` is truthy (line 131). An attacker who obtains a single valid backup code can send `backupCode=<valid>` plus `totpCode=<any-non-empty-string>`; the first check is skipped because totpCode is truthy, the second branch succeeds on the backup code alone, and login returns without ever verifying the password. Stolen backup codes (which users download as plaintext `cal-backup-codes.txt`) therefore become password-equivalent. Require password verification for CAL users on every credentials login, independent of which second factor is supplied.

findings.title: Backup-code consume is non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts the backup-code login does read-decrypt-indexOf then a separate `prisma.user.update` that writes `backupCodes[index]=null` back (lines 139-156). Two concurrent logins with the same code can both read the same array, both find the same index, and both succeed before either write nulls it, allowing single-use codes to be reused. Use an atomic transaction/conditional update so consumption cannot race.

findings.title: Backup-code matching only strips dashes, crashes on non-string
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 (same pattern in next-auth-options.ts line 144) the code does `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` and `indexOf` against lowercase hex codes generated in setup.ts. It does not trim whitespace/newlines from copy-paste, does not case-fold uppercase hex, and assumes a string so an array/object value throws TypeError resulting in a 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. Valid user-entered codes are rejected and malformed input crashes the handler. Normalize with String(), trim(), toLowerCase() and validate type before comparing.

findings.title: API throws instead of returning JSON error
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts the new backup-code branches (and existing secret branches) do `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when the encryption key is missing or the secret is corrupt (lines 51,77,82,90). An uncaught throw in a Next.js API route returns HTML 500, not the `{error: ErrorCode}` JSON the frontend expects (`await response.json()` then fails), so callers get `something_went_wrong` via exception path and logs lose structured handling. Return `res.status(500).json({error: ...})` like the other branches.

findings.title: No test for login or disable with backup code
findings.body: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the PR only tests backup-code download/copy UI after enable and leaves `TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. The security-critical paths added here — login via `credentials.backupCode` including single-use invalidation (`backupCodes[index]=null`), and disable via backup code — have zero automated coverage, so regressions like reuse, wrong-code handling, or MissingBackupCodes would ship undetected. Add e2e tests that log in with a backup code, verify it cannot be reused, and disable 2FA with a backup code.
